label_policy.accept: A real, high-value defect reachable through the supported product input path.
label_policy.downgrade: A technically sound robustness improvement with little or no reachable user impact.
label_policy.reject: Expected behavior, low-value diagnostics, or a scenario outside the producer contract.

findings.title: Uninitialized array-destructuring const crashes the parser
findings.supervision: The parser must diagnose this valid frontend input consistently with TypeScript semantics instead of crashing. The analysis is correct and the defect is valuable.

findings.title: MergeDataSection requires non-overlapping AS data segments
findings.supervision: The analysis identifies a valid internal invariant, but normal AssemblyScript output does not contain overlapping segments. An assertion is sufficient; do not present this as a user-impacting compiler bug.

findings.title: Closure lowering removes a potentially trapping argument
findings.supervision: Removing this trap is intended by the compiler design, so it is not a bug. The observation points to a missing comment or design document and should be reported only as documentation debt.

findings.title: ConditionalReturn can generate a colliding nested block label
findings.supervision: The collision requires hand-written WAT with a label shape Warpo does not generate. Reject it unless a supported AssemblyScript source reproducer reaches the pass.

findings.title: Object-literal accessor initialization order
findings.supervision: Valid source code produces an incorrect value and violates source evaluation order. The analysis is correct, has a runtime oracle, and is a valuable compiler bug.

findings.title: Global array bindings emit the same unsupported-feature error twice
findings.supervision: The unsupported construct is already rejected and diagnostics may be emitted at multiple ownership layers. Robustness is not impaired, so duplicate logging alone is too low-value to report.

findings.title: ConstructorNewOutlining allocation operand issues
findings.supervision: AssemblyScript fixes class id and allocation size for a given constructor and does not emit the proposed caller-local allocation form. Reject synthetic IR that violates those frontend invariants.

findings.title: Immutable-load folding uses the wrong byte for overlapping data segments
findings.supervision: Warpo does not generate overlapping active data segments. A hand-written WAT counterexample is outside this pass's producer contract and is not a Warpo defect.
